subject: Pilot runway options: staggered runway + true-up vs top-up credits
messages:
From: Claire Atwood <claire@brightharbor.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>
Cc: Edward Mills <procurement@brightharbor.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask — pilot runway and spike in usage

Hi Markus,

Quick note from our side — the pilot has been going well, but after last week's user demo the usage spiked ~3x vs our forecast (see attached). We love the latency and output quality so far.

We have ~10 days left on the initial time-boxed eval and procurement is asking whether we can either: (A) add a small top-up of tokens to cover the surge, or (B) extend the pilot by two weeks while we finish feature validation.

Procurement is sensitive to open-ended extensions; they prefer a capped runway with a true-up if we exceed thresholds. Can you propose a quick two-option approach (top-up vs capped extension + true-up) and include any price impact? We need something to present to Edward by Friday.

Thanks,
Claire

[Attachment: BrightHarbor_MVP_usage_report.csv (csv, 42KB)]

From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Atwood <claire@brightharbor.ai>
Cc: Edward Mills <procurement@brightharbor.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot runway and spike in usage

Hi Claire — thanks for the heads-up and the report. Happy to put two concrete options on the table. High level: we can do (1) a one-off credit top-up that covers the measured overage, or (2) a 14-day capped runway extension with a tiered true-up if usage goes beyond an agreed monthly cap.

Option 1 — Top-up credit
- $X equivalent token credit to cover the ~3x burst (one-time)
- No term change; pilot end date stays the same

Option 2 — Staggered runway + true-up (recommended for validation)
- 14-day extension to the pilot with a capped daily token allotment (we propose 120% of your current daily avg)
- If cumulative usage exceeds the cap, we'll true-up at standard pilot rate with a 10% rebate on the overage (applies once total overage > 20%)
- Includes standard Pilot SLA and support level

I can put these in a short term sheet. Laura — can you confirm whether Legal is comfortable with the 10% rebate language and whether we can push a small service-fee waiver? Ben — any pricing guidance if BrightHarbor elects Option 2?

-Markus

Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
markus.k@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0147

[Attachment: Redwood_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (pdf, 98KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot runway and spike in usage

Markus — sounds reasonable. A few notes from Legal/Commercial:
- "10% rebate on the overage" is OK if we limit it to once cumulative overage exceeds 20% of the agreed cap (keeps exposure bounded).
- We should avoid language that implies credits are automatic — make it contingent on mutually agreed usage reporting at the end of the extension.
- Approve a small one-time service-fee waiver (we typically cap at one waiver per customer per year).

Pricing note for Ben: recommend we present Option 2 with a modest discount on the true-up rate (15% off list) if they commit to a conversion conversation at the end of the pilot. If they want a purely open-ended extension, push back.

Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask — pilot runway and spike in usage

Agree with Laura. Two quick alternatives for framing the price options to BrightHarbor:
A) Clean top-up credit: calculate the delta from forecast -> bill that at pilot unit rate, give 5% courtesy credit for the disruption.
B) Staggered runway (preferred): 14-day extension with capped daily allotment, true-up at 85% of list if they sign a 6-month conversion within 30 days. That gives them predictability + an incentive to convert.

If they push for lower, we can offer a one-time 10% discount on the true-up but require a minimum committed monthly capacity post-conversion.

Ben Carter
Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Atwood <claire@brightharbor.ai>
Cc: Edward Mills <procurement@brightharbor.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.b@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.c@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Oct 2025 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: two-path runway solution for BrightHarbor pilot

Claire / Edward — thank you. Below are the two options we recommend; I've kept each concise so procurement can review quickly.

Option A — Top-up credit (fast)
- One-time token credit to cover measured overage per attached usage report
- Billed at pilot unit rate; Redwood extends a 5% courtesy credit on that overage amount
- No change to pilot end date or terms

Option B — Staggered runway + true-up (recommended)
- 14-day extension starting 2025-10-16
- Daily cap = 120% of your average daily usage over the last 14 days
- If total usage across the 14 days exceeds the cap by >20%, we true-up the overage at the pilot unit rate with a 15% discount.
- If BrightHarbor signs a 6-month conversion within 30 days of pilot end, Redwood will apply a further one-time 10% conversion credit toward the first invoice.
- Standard pilot SLA and one service-fee waiver included

Next steps: pick A or B and we'll generate a short addendum + DocuSign link for Edward. If you choose B, we will send an updated term sheet that includes the daily cap and reporting cadence.

Thanks,
Markus

[Attachment: Redwood_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (pdf, 98KB)]

From: Claire Atwood <claire@brightharbor.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.k@redwood.ai>
Cc: Edward Mills <procurement@brightharbor.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: two-path runway solution for BrightHarbor pilot

Thanks Markus — BrightHarbor will take Option B (staggered runway + true-up). A couple of procurement asks before we sign:
1) Please include a one-sentence SLA summary in the addendum (availability target + escalation contact).
2) Edward requests the DocuSign bundle include the updated term sheet and a short summary of the true-up calculation.
3) We need an itemized estimate of the potential true-up cost bands (low/med/high) so Finance can pre-approve.

If you can get those in the DocuSign package, Edward will run it through procurement and we should be able to return a countersigned copy within 48 hours.

Claire
